title: What Are the World's Happiest Destinations
paragraphs: Where do travelers feel the happiest? According to a new study, the answer is Tulum, a beach town in Mexico.

The study was done by JustCover, a travel insurance company in Ireland, and it was published in July 2026. The company looked at more than one million online reviews of tourist attractions, resorts, national parks and beautiful places in 155 destinations. It searched the reviews for words that showed happiness, such as "this place made me so happy." Then it gave each place a score. The place with the most happy reviews got a score of 100.

Tulum was first. It is famous for its beaches and old Mayan ruins. In second place was Soufrière, in Saint Lucia, a Caribbean island, with a score of 95.2. Oaxaca, in Mexico, and Las Vegas, in the United States, were tied for third place, with a score of 88.0.

The United States did very well in the study. Maui, in Hawaii, was fifth, New York City was sixth and Chicago was ninth. Other places in the top 10 were Cappadocia in Turkey, Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, and Toronto in Canada and the Maldives, which tied for 10th place. In Europe, the happiest place was Positano, in Italy, which was 16th in the world.

However, there are some problems with the study. It only counted reviews that used clear words about happiness. Also, people usually write reviews about vacation places, not places they just pass through. So, the study measures what people write online, not how happy they really are. In addition, many of the reviews were written several years ago, so they may not show what these places are like today.
